key_insight: Agent-driven query reshaping makes simple retrieval (e.g., keyword/grep-style) far more effective in agentic workflows—matching or exceeding complex RAG pipelines on many tasks while lowering cost and latency.
problem_solved: Provides a systematic comparison of retrieval strategies in agentic search and shows how retrieval choice interacts with agent architecture and tool-calling, filling a gap in guidance for building efficient, accurate tool-using agents.
method: Benchmark diverse retrieval strategies (sparse/grep, dense embeddings, hybrid, reranking) across multiple agent architectures and tool-calling paradigms.
Introduce and evaluate Agentic Reshaping: an agent-driven loop that reformulates queries, selects/filters chunks, and adapts retrieval to downstream tools.
Measure tradeoffs in accuracy, latency, and cost on representative agentic tasks to identify practical deployment recommendations.
impact: Shows practitioners they can often substitute expensive RAG stacks with lightweight retrieval plus agentic query reshaping to achieve similar or better performance—saving compute and simplifying system design.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: Agentic Reshaping loop (user prompt → query reformulation → retrieval → tool call → result refinement).
Bar chart: Accuracy vs cost/latency for grep/sparse, dense, hybrid, and RAG approaches across tasks.
Heatmap/matrix: Interaction effects between retrieval strategy, agent architecture, and tool-calling paradigm.
Icons: speed (clock), cost (dollar), accuracy (target) to quickly convey tradeoffs.
paper_title: Is Grep All You Need? How Agent Harnesses Reshape Agentic Search
paper_authors: Sahil Sen, Akhil Kasturi, Elias Lumer, Anmol Gulati, Vamse Kumar Subbiah
